title: Add Custom Fields to WooCommerce Checkout
description:
To add a custom field to a WooCommerce checkout you need three hooks for the data path and two for display: woocommerce_after_checkout_billing_form prints the input, woocommerce_after_checkout_validation rejects bad values, woocommerce_checkout_update_order_meta saves it, and then woocommerce_admin_order_data_after_billing_address and woocommerce_email_order_meta_fields put it on the order screen and in the emails. The popular version of that recipe does all five and still loses the value on a shop running HPOS, because it writes to post meta and trusts the request.

Below is the snippet as it usually appears, then a refactor in four steps with the reason for each change. You need WooCommerce active and somewhere to put PHP. A small plugin or an mu-plugin beats functions.php here, because the field is order data and should outlive a theme switch.

The snippet most people start with, and what it actually stores

This is close to the first thing you find for the search, and it looks fine on a test order placed by the person who wrote it.

add_action( 'woocommerce_after_checkout_billing_form', function () {
    echo '<p class="form-row"><label for="delivery_note">Delivery note</label>';
    echo '<input type="text" id="delivery_note" name="delivery_note" />';
    echo '</p>';
} );

add_action( 'woocommerce_checkout_update_order_meta', function ( $order_id ) {
    update_post_meta( $order_id, 'delivery_note', $_POST['delivery_note'] );
} );

add_action( 'woocommerce_admin_order_data_after_billing_address', function ( $order ) {
    echo '<p><strong>Delivery note:</strong> ' . get_post_meta( $order->get_id(), 'delivery_note', true ) . '</p>';
} );

Four things are wrong with it, and none of them show up on the first checkout.

update_post_meta() writes to wp_postmeta. Orders lived there for years, so this worked. With HPOS an order is a row in wc_orders and its meta is in wc_orders_meta, and $order->get_meta() never looks at post meta. On an HPOS store WooCommerce keeps a placeholder row in wp_posts with the same ID, so update_post_meta() and get_post_meta() still find each other and the order screen shows the note. Everything that reads the order the supported way does not: $order->get_meta(), the REST API, exports and other plugins all see nothing. The HPOS custom order meta migration post goes further into what to do with orders created before the switch.

The second problem is $_POST['delivery_note'] read without checking it exists. On the block checkout, or when another plugin removes the field, PHP raises "Undefined array key" on every order. With WP_DEBUG_DISPLAY on, that warning is printed into the checkout AJAX response and the spinner never resolves.

Third, nothing is sanitised. A customer can type <script> into a text input, it goes into the database as typed, and it comes back out as typed on the order screen. That is stored XSS aimed at whoever opens the order, usually a shop manager with more capabilities than the customer. Emails are less exposed because WooCommerce runs the value through wp_kses_post(); the admin screen is not.

The snippet above on an HPOS store, after a customer typed a note with a script tag in it (test site: WordPress 7.1.3, WooCommerce 11.2.2 with HPOS on, PHP 8.2):

Order #13, HPOS on: yes
get_post_meta( id, 'delivery_note' ):    'Leave by the door <script>alert(document.cookie)</script>'
$order->get_meta( 'delivery_note' ):     ''
$order->get_meta( '_wpth_delivery_note' ): ''
Order screen prints: <p><strong>Delivery note:</strong> Leave by the door <script>alert(document.cookie)</script></p>

The order screen line is exactly what a shop manager's browser receives: the script tag runs as soon as they open the order.

Fourth, there is no length limit and no validation, so a 4,000 character paste ends up on a picking slip. The hand-written markup also misses the label association and the classes the rest of the form uses, which is why the field looks pasted in.

woocommerce_form_field gives you the wrapper, the label and the styling 

add_action( 'woocommerce_after_checkout_billing_form', 'wpth_render_delivery_note_field' );

function wpth_render_delivery_note_field( $checkout ) {
    woocommerce_form_field(
        'wpth_delivery_note',
        array(
            'type'              => 'text',
            'label'             => __( 'Delivery note', 'wpth' ),
            'placeholder'       => __( 'Gate code, safe place, neighbour', 'wpth' ),
            'required'          => false,
            'class'             => array( 'form-row-wide' ),
            'custom_attributes' => array(
                'maxlength'    => '200',
                'autocomplete' => 'off',
            ),
        ),
        $checkout->get_value( 'wpth_delivery_note' )
    );
}

woocommerce_form_field() is the helper WooCommerce uses for its own billing inputs. You pass a key, an argument array and a value, and it builds the form-row wrapper, the label with a matching for, the input-text class and the placeholder. The field then lines up with the rest of the form and inherits whatever styling the theme applies to checkout inputs.

The third argument is the current value. Passing $checkout->get_value( 'wpth_delivery_note' ) lets WooCommerce repopulate the input from the posted data when the checkout is re-rendered after a validation error, so the customer does not retype the gate code.

The classic checkout with the delivery note field at the end of the billing details (test site: WordPress 7.1.3, WooCommerce 11.2.2 with HPOS on, PHP 8.2)

maxlength goes in custom_attributes because that array is rendered straight onto the input element. Treat it as a hint for the browser, not a rule: anyone can remove it in devtools, which is why the next step repeats the limit on the server.

Where to validate: woocommerce_after_checkout_validation, not the render callback 

add_action( 'woocommerce_after_checkout_validation', 'wpth_validate_delivery_note', 10, 2 );

function wpth_validate_delivery_note( $data, $errors ) {
    if ( ! isset( $_POST['wpth_delivery_note'] ) ) {
        return;
    }

    $raw  = wp_unslash( $_POST['wpth_delivery_note'] );
    $note = is_string( $raw ) ? sanitize_text_field( $raw ) : '';

    if ( is_string( $raw ) && '' !== trim( $raw ) && '' === $note ) {
        $errors->add(
            'wpth_delivery_note_unreadable',
            __( 'That delivery note could not be read. Please type it again.', 'wpth' )
        );
        return;
    }

    if ( mb_strlen( $note ) > 200 ) {
        $errors->add(
            'wpth_delivery_note_length',
            __( 'Please keep the delivery note under 200 characters.', 'wpth' )
        );
    }

    if ( preg_match( '#https?://#i', $note ) ) {
        $errors->add(
            'wpth_delivery_note_url',
            __( 'Please do not put links in the delivery note.', 'wpth' )
        );
    }
}

woocommerce_checkout_process is the hook most snippets use, and it works: add a notice with type error and checkout stops. woocommerce_after_checkout_validation is the better place because it hands you a WP_Error object and runs after WooCommerce has checked its own fields, so you add one message instead of racing the core checks.

The $data argument is not the whole request. WC_Checkout::get_posted_data() builds it from the fields registered through woocommerce_checkout_fields, so a field added with woocommerce_after_checkout_billing_form is not in there. Read $_POST and treat it as hostile.

wp_unslash() comes first because WordPress slashes every superglobal on load; sanitising comes second. The is_string() guard makes the intent explicit. A request with wpth_delivery_note[]=x posts an array; sanitize_text_field() turns an array into an empty string rather than failing, so without the guard an array would quietly become an empty note. With it, you decide.

woocommerce_after_checkout_validation run against four inputs (test site: WordPress 7.1.3, WooCommerce 11.2.2 with HPOS on, PHP 8.2):

a 250-character note   -> Please keep the delivery note under 200 characters.
a note with a link     -> Please do not put links in the delivery note.
an array (note[]=x)    -> accepted
a normal note          -> accepted

sanitize_text_field( array( 'x' ) ) returns: ''

$errors->add() takes a code and a message. The code is what you grep for later, so make it unique to the field rather than reusing invalid_postcode. To see the error path without a real payment, submit the checkout with a 250 character note: the notice appears above the payment box and no order is created.

Saving through the order object is what keeps the value under HPOS 

add_action( 'woocommerce_checkout_update_order_meta', 'wpth_save_delivery_note', 10, 2 );

function wpth_save_delivery_note( $order_id, $data ) {
    if ( ! isset( $_POST['wpth_delivery_note'] ) ) {
        return;
    }

    $raw  = wp_unslash( $_POST['wpth_delivery_note'] );
    $note = is_string( $raw ) ? sanitize_text_field( $raw ) : '';

    $order = wc_get_order( $order_id );

    if ( ! $order ) {
        return;
    }

    if ( '' === $note ) {
        $order->delete_meta_data( '_wpth_delivery_note' );
    } else {
        $order->update_meta_data( '_wpth_delivery_note', $note );
    }

    $order->save();
}

wc_get_order() returns the order whichever storage is active, and update_meta_data() followed by save() writes to the right table. That is the whole HPOS fix: no update_post_meta(), no get_post_meta(), no branching on which storage the shop uses.

The _wpth_ prefix avoids collisions with other plugins, and the leading underscore hides the key from the legacy custom fields box, which is what you want for a value the customer should not edit from the order screen.

Deleting on empty matters more than it looks. Without it, a customer who clears the field on a second attempt leaves the old note attached, and the warehouse reads a gate code that no longer applies.

The same script-tag note saved through the order object, and read back (test site: WordPress 7.1.3, WooCommerce 11.2.2 with HPOS on, PHP 8.2):

Order #13, HPOS on: yes
get_post_meta( id, 'delivery_note' ):    ''
$order->get_meta( 'delivery_note' ):     ''
$order->get_meta( '_wpth_delivery_note' ): 'Leave by the door'
Order screen prints: <p class="wpth-delivery-note"><strong>Delivery note</strong><br />Leave by the door</p>

sanitize_text_field() removed the tag on the way in, and the order screen line is plain text.

woocommerce_checkout_create_order is the other place to save. It passes the order object before it is written, so you call $order->update_meta_data() and let WooCommerce do the save(). Either hook works; woocommerce_checkout_update_order_meta passes the ID, which is why older snippets use it.

The order screen and the emails need two separate display hooks 

add_action( 'woocommerce_admin_order_data_after_billing_address', 'wpth_show_delivery_note_in_admin' );

function wpth_show_delivery_note_in_admin( $order ) {
    $note = $order->get_meta( '_wpth_delivery_note' );

    if ( '' === $note ) {
        return;
    }

    printf(
        '<p class="wpth-delivery-note"><strong>%s</strong><br />%s</p>',
        esc_html__( 'Delivery note', 'wpth' ),
        esc_html( $note )
    );
}

add_filter( 'woocommerce_email_order_meta_fields', 'wpth_add_delivery_note_to_emails', 10, 3 );

function wpth_add_delivery_note_to_emails( $fields, $sent_to_admin, $order ) {
    $note = $order->get_meta( '_wpth_delivery_note' );

    if ( '' === $note ) {
        return $fields;
    }

    $fields['wpth_delivery_note'] = array(
        'label' => __( 'Delivery note', 'wpth' ),
        'value' => $note,
    );

    return $fields;
}

woocommerce_admin_order_data_after_billing_address fires inside the billing box on both the legacy order screen and the HPOS one, so the note sits where the person packing the parcel is already looking. esc_html() on the way out is the second half of the XSS fix: sanitising on save protects new orders, escaping on output protects the ones already in the database with a script tag in them.

woocommerce_email_order_meta_fields adds a row to the order details table in every WooCommerce email, customer and admin. The $sent_to_admin argument is there if you want the note only in the admin copy. The value is printed through wp_kses_post(), so a stray bracket will not break the email layout, but that is not a substitute for sanitising at save time.

For the customer-facing side, woocommerce_order_details_after_order_table prints the same value on the thank-you page and under My Account. Same get_meta() call, same escaping.

The email field the filter adds (same test site):

Email fields: {"wpth_delivery_note":{"label":"Delivery note","value":"Leave by the door"}}

The HPOS order edit screen with the delivery note under the billing address (test site: WordPress 7.1.3, WooCommerce 11.2.2 with HPOS on, PHP 8.2)

The block checkout never runs woocommerce_after_checkout_billing_form

If the Checkout page contains the Checkout block instead of the [woocommerce_checkout] shortcode, none of the rendering above happens. The block is rendered by React from the Store API, and the classic form hooks do not exist in that tree. New WooCommerce installs create block checkout pages, so this is the default on a fresh shop rather than an edge case.

The supported route is the Additional Checkout Fields API, available since WooCommerce 8.9.

add_action( 'woocommerce_init', 'wpth_register_delivery_note_block_field' );

function wpth_register_delivery_note_block_field() {
    if ( ! function_exists( 'woocommerce_register_additional_checkout_field' ) ) {
        return;
    }

    woocommerce_register_additional_checkout_field(
        array(
            'id'       => 'wpth/delivery-note',
            'label'    => __( 'Delivery note', 'wpth' ),
            'location' => 'order',
            'type'     => 'text',
            'required' => false,
        )
    );
}

The id has to be namespaced, location decides where the field appears (contact, address or order), and type is text, select or checkbox. WooCommerce renders it, validates it and saves it. The value lands in order meta under _wc_other/ followed by the field id, so $order->get_meta( '_wc_other/wpth/delivery-note' ) reads it back and the admin and email callbacks above work once you point them at that key. If the key looks different on your install, dump $order->get_meta_data() once and read it off.

Whether these fields also appear in the shortcode checkout depends on your WooCommerce version, so test both before deleting the classic hooks. Registering the field while the classic callbacks are still active is safe, because the block checkout ignores the classic ones.

The block checkout with the delivery note registered through the Additional Checkout Fields API (test site: WordPress 7.1.3, WooCommerce 11.2.2 with HPOS on, PHP 8.2)

The meta WooCommerce writes when the block checkout saves the field (same test site):

meta key _billing_address_index =           
meta key _shipping_address_index =          
meta key _wc_other/wpth/delivery-note = Leave at the back door

Checking the saved value from the command line

When the field saves but does not display, or displays but does not save, the question is which half is broken. Read the meta straight off the order:

wp eval '
$order = wc_get_order( 123 );
echo $order->get_meta( "_wpth_delivery_note" ), PHP_EOL;
'

An empty result means the save hook did not run, so check which checkout form is actually rendering. A value here with nothing on the order screen means the display callback is attached to something that is not being rendered, usually a legacy meta box on a store that has moved to HPOS.

If customers cannot get past the shipping step at all, that is a different problem: no shipping options available in WooCommerce walks through it.

One follow-up worth the time: put the note in the orders list so nobody opens each order to read it. On HPOS the column filter is woocommerce_shop_order_list_table_columns and the render hook is woocommerce_shop_order_list_table_custom_column; on the legacy list it is manage_edit-shop_order_columns with manage_shop_order_posts_custom_column. Two callbacks, one get_meta() call, and the packing bench stops clicking.

Originally published on WP Tuts Hub.

title: Docker Explained for Backend Developers
description:
As a backend developer(like me), you probably spend most of your time writing application logic, building APIs, connecting databases, handling authentication, and making sure everything works as expected.

But there is another important part of backend development: deployment.

You have built your application, tested it locally, and everything works. Now you need to move it to a server. This is where things can become complicated.

The server may have a different Python version, missing dependencies, a different environment configuration, or other software conflicts.

Docker helps solve many of these problems.

1. What Is Docker?

Docker is a platform that allows you to package an application together with the dependencies and configuration it needs to run. This package is called a container.

For example, imagine you have built a Django application that requires:

  • Python 3.12
  • Django
  • PostgreSQL client libraries
  • Some Python packages
  • Environment variables

Instead of manually installing and configuring everything on every server, you can define the application environment using Docker.

You can then build an image and run it as a container on another machine with Docker installed.

The idea is simple: your application should run in a consistent environment, regardless of where you deploy it.

2. Understanding Images and Containers

These two terms are important when learning Docker.

Docker Image: An image is the packaged blueprint used to create a container. It contains the application code, dependencies, and instructions needed to run it.

Docker Container: A container is a running instance of an image.

Think of an image as a recipe and a container as the actual meal prepared from that recipe. You can create multiple containers from the same image.

3. Creating a Dockerfile

Let's use a simple FastAPI application as an example.

Imagine your project has this structure:

my-api/
├── main.py
├── requirements.txt
└── Dockerfile

Your requirements.txt could contain:

fastapi
uvicorn

Now, create a file called Dockerfile:

FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

COPY requirements.txt .

RUN pip install --no-cache-dir -r requirements.txt

COPY . .

EXPOSE 8000

CMD ["uvicorn", "main:app", "--host", "0.0.0.0", "--port", "8000"]

Let's understand each instruction.

  • FROM python:3.12-slim: Specifies the base image. We are using a lightweight Python 3.12 image.
  • WORKDIR /app: Sets /app as the working directory inside the container.
  • COPY requirements.txt .: Copies the requirements file into the container.
  • RUN pip install ...: Installs the Python dependencies.
  • COPY . .: Copies the rest of the application files into the container.
  • EXPOSE 8000: Documents that the application listens on port 8000.
  • CMD [...]: Defines the command that runs when the container starts.

Notice that we use 0.0.0.0 as the host. This allows the application to accept connections from outside the container.

4. Building and Running the Container

Once your Dockerfile is ready, open your terminal in the project directory.

Build the image:

docker build -t my-api .

Here:

  • docker build builds an image.
  • -t my-api gives the image a name.
  • . tells Docker to use the current directory as the build context.

Now run the container:

docker run -d -p 8000:8000 --name my-api-container my-api

What does this command do?

  • docker run creates and starts a container.
  • -d runs it in the background.
  • -p 8000:8000 maps port 8000 on your machine to port 8000 inside the container.
  • --name gives the container a name.
  • my-api specifies the image to run.

You can now access the API through:

http://localhost:8000

5. Why Docker Matters for Backend Deployment

This is where Docker becomes particularly useful to backend developers.

When deploying an application without containers, you may need to manually configure the server, install the right runtime, install dependencies, and manage different versions of software.

With Docker, you can package the application environment and deploy it as a container.

For example, you can:

  • Build your application image locally.
  • Push the image to a container registry such as Docker Hub or Amazon ECR.
  • Pull that image on your production server.
  • Start the application using the same environment you tested.

This makes deployments more predictable and reduces problems caused by differences between development and production environments.

It also makes it easier to roll out new application versions and roll back when something goes wrong.

6. Docker Compose: Running Your Backend and Database Together

Most backend applications need more than one service.

A typical application may have:

  • A Django or FastAPI backend.
  • A PostgreSQL database.
  • A Redis instance for caching or background tasks.

Docker Compose allows you to define and manage multiple containers using one configuration file.

For example:

services:
  backend:
    build: .
    ports:
      - "8000:8000"
    depends_on:
      - db

  db:
    image: postgres:16
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: myapp
      POSTGRES_USER: admin
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
    volumes:
      - postgres_data:/var/lib/postgresql/data

volumes:
  postgres_data:

You can start both services with:

docker compose up -d

Docker Compose creates and starts the containers based on the configuration.

The database also has a named volume, which helps preserve its data when the container is replaced.

7. Docker and DevOps

Docker is one of the tools that connects backend development with DevOps.

As a backend developer, understanding Docker means you are not limited to writing code and handing it over to someone else for deployment.

You can understand how your application is packaged, how its dependencies are managed, how it communicates with other services, and how it runs in production.

It also prepares you for other DevOps tools and practices, including:

  • CI/CD: Automatically building and testing Docker images whenever code changes.
  • Container registries: Storing and distributing application images.
  • Cloud deployment: Running containers on AWS, Azure, and other platforms.
  • Kubernetes: Managing containers across multiple machines.
  • Infrastructure automation: Provisioning the infrastructure required to run your applications.

Conclusion

Docker is not just about running applications inside containers. It is about making applications easier to package, move, test, and deploy.

For backend developers, this is especially important because building an application is only one part of the job. Understanding how to get that application running reliably in production is equally valuable.

You don't necessarily need to become a DevOps engineer to benefit from Docker. But if you understand Docker, you become a backend developer who understands more of the application lifecycle, from writing the code to getting it running on a server.

title: I Built a Candle That Burns Down in Real-Time as the Year Passes
description:
Hi everyone! I'm Marcos, an independent digital creator from Venezuela. Today I want to share a small project I built entirely from scratch: a web page where a candle slowly consumes itself second by second, showing exactly how much time is left until the New Year.

The Idea

I wanted to create something visual, calming, and slightly philosophical — a way to feel the year passing by instead of just reading a countdown. So I built The Year Candle: a single web page where a green candle with a golden holder burns down mathematically, in perfect sync with the calendar.

How It Works

The math is simple but elegant. The script calculates the percentage of the year that has already passed (from January 1st to December 31st) and applies that percentage to the height of the candle. Every second, the candle shrinks a tiny bit. By the time December 31st at 11:59:59 PM arrives, the candle is completely gone.

The best part? It works automatically for every visitor in their own local timezone. Someone in Tokyo, someone in Madrid, and someone in Caracas all see the candle burning according to their own clock. No server, no database, just pure client-side JavaScript.

Features I'm Proud Of

  • A "ghost" shadow behind the candle shows the original full height, so you can visually see how much has been consumed.
  • A flickering green flame with occasional magical sparks that rise from it.
  • Wax drips that slowly slide down the sides of the candle.
  • Automatic New Year celebration: when the clock strikes midnight on December 31st, the page detects the year change without reloading, fireworks explode across the screen, the new year number appears big at the top, slides down, and the candle rebuilds itself from scratch to start burning again for the new year.
  • A donate button in the corner, because I'm trying to build a sustainable path as an independent creator.

The Tech Stack

Just the classics, no frameworks:

  • HTML5 for the structure
  • CSS3 with gradients, animations, and keyframes for all the visuals
  • Vanilla JavaScript for the math, the canvas-based fireworks, and the automatic year detection

I also split the code into three separate files (index.html, css/style.css, js/script.js) to keep things clean and maintainable. The whole project is hosted for free on GitHub Pages.

Try It Yourself

You can watch the candle burning right now at:
👉 The Year Candle

Support My Work

I'm building small, useful, and aesthetic digital experiences, one project at a time. If you enjoyed this or found it interesting, you can support my independent work here:
☕ Buy me a coffee on Ko-fi

What's Next

I'm planning to build more mini web tools — a breathing guide, a focus timer, maybe an interactive map. If you have ideas or suggestions, I'd love to hear them in the comments.

Thanks for reading, and happy coding! 🕯️✨

title: Why your prompt cache never hits, and what it saves
description:
A prompt cache pays only when the start of every request is identical and calls come often enough. The usual reasons it misses, and a way to check.

A prompt cache lets the API remember the beginning of a request, so the next request that starts with exactly the same text does not pay full price to process it again. When it works, repeated calls get cheaper and start answering sooner. When it does not, you pay for the marks you added and get nothing back, and no error tells you so. The only sign is a usage counter that stays at zero. This guide explains what has to be true for a hit, the five ordinary reasons for a miss, and a short routine for finding out which one applies to you.

title: From Localhost to Live: My Full-Stack Task Management Application Deployment Journey
description:
Building a web application is not only about writing code. Making it accessible to users through the internet is equally important. During my Full-Stack Web Development Internship at Valentius Kryptix, I worked on developing and deploying a Task Management Application. This project helped me understand how frontend, backend, database, authentication, and hosting work together in a real-world application.

Project Overview

The main objective was to create a web application where users can register, log in, and manage their daily tasks. Users can create new tasks, view existing tasks, update task details, and delete tasks whenever required.

I developed the frontend using React.js, which provides an interactive and user-friendly interface. For the backend, I used Node.js and Express.js to create REST APIs and handle application requests.

Technology Stack

The project involved several technologies:

  • React.js: For frontend development and user interaction.
  • Node.js: For backend runtime.
  • Express.js: For creating RESTful APIs.
  • MongoDB Atlas: For storing user and task information in a cloud database.
  • JWT Authentication: For securing user sessions and protecting API routes.
  • Vercel: For frontend deployment.
  • Render: For backend hosting.

Understanding Full-Stack Integration

One of the most important parts of this project was connecting all application components.

The React frontend communicates with the Express backend through API requests. The backend processes these requests and interacts with MongoDB Atlas to store or retrieve information.

I also implemented JWT-based authentication. After a successful login, the server generates a token that is used when accessing protected routes. This helps ensure that users can manage only their authorized resources.

The application supports CRUD operations: Create, Read, Update, and Delete. These operations form the foundation of many real-world applications.

Deployment and Challenges

Deployment was an important learning experience. I deployed the frontend through Vercel and hosted the backend using Render. MongoDB Atlas was configured as the cloud database.

During deployment, I faced challenges involving database connections, environment variables, API integration, authentication, and frontend routing. I also had to resolve configuration issues to ensure that the application worked correctly after deployment.

Testing the live application was essential. I checked registration, login, and task operations to verify that the frontend, backend, and database communicated properly.

Key Learnings

This project improved my understanding of full-stack development and production deployment. I gained practical experience in building REST APIs, connecting cloud databases, implementing authentication, debugging errors, and deploying applications.

It also taught me that successful software development requires patience, problem-solving, and continuous testing.

Conclusion

Working on this Task Management Application during my internship at Valentius Kryptix was a valuable experience. It gave me confidence in developing and deploying complete web applications and motivated me to explore more real-world development projects.

title: Node.js Content-Aware Crops — Store Multiple Aspect-Ratio Variants After Moderation
description:
A gaming catalog cannot treat a visually good crop as a publishable crop. Moderation coverage is the operational constraint: approve the source image first, then run a content-aware crop for every known display ratio during ingest, store each result, and retain the original for the slot the product team has not designed yet. Do not crop on the read path. That choice keeps storefront latency predictable and prevents one source asset from producing variants under different policy decisions.

TL;DR: enumerate the real render slots, run one moderation decision before transformation, derive the approved variants once, and publish a manifest only after every required crop has been stored. Keep the source private. This costs more storage than request-time transformation, but it gives the serving tier a small, bounded job and makes quarantine behavior comprehensible.

How should Node.js crop content-aware variants for multiple aspect ratios?

Consider a bounded production scenario rather than a benchmark: a seller submits one product photo for a game marketplace, background removal has already isolated the item, and the storefront needs square search tiles, portrait detail cards, and wide promotional rails. The dangerous outcome is not merely a face or logo landing outside the crop. It is an image becoming reachable while its moderation result is absent, ambiguous, or attached to a different derivative.

I would set the ingest invariant this way: no manifest becomes readable until the source has one accepted moderation decision and all three declared variants have durable object keys. A rejected or undecided source yields zero published variants. The original remains private because a later 5:7 slot should be derived from the same reviewed input, not from a lossy 1:1 child.

Three aspect ratios are an example capacity envelope, not a universal constant. The important number is the count of actual UI slots. Ten speculative ratios multiply writes, storage, invalidation work, and the moderation evidence that operators must trace during an appeal. One ratio derived at request time creates the opposite problem: CPU and upstream latency move into the user-facing SLO. In an Express service, the upload route shouldn't wait for those multiple content-aware crop calls; it should enqueue immutable work and let a bounded worker store each variant.

Short paths win.

The ingest state machine

Treat this as a state transition, not a controller that fires several unrelated promises. The source moves through received, moderating, deriving, and ready; quarantined is terminal until a new review event. Only ready has a serving manifest. If a crop write fails, retry that deterministic object key and leave the manifest unpublished.

The following Go client shows the less comfortable but safer boundary. It uses the public discovery endpoint to inspect the live request schema, accepts request JSON prepared against that schema, sends every call with an explicit method and the same key, and backs off on HTTP 429. This avoids baking guessed fields into infrastructure code. Run it once with CAPABILITY=image.moderate and a matching REQUEST_JSON; only after that response is accepted by the pipeline should the worker run it for image.smart_crop once per ratio. The application, rather than an accidental chain of callbacks, owns that handoff and the final publication barrier.

package main

import (
    "bytes"
    "fmt"
    "io"
    "net/http"
    "os"
    "strconv"
    "time"
)

func request(method, path string, body []byte, authenticated bool) ([]byte, error) {
    baseURL := os.Getenv("INFRAI_BASE_URL")
    if baseURL == "" { panic("set INFRAI_BASE_URL to the documented v1 base URL") }
    for attempt := 0; attempt < 5; attempt++ {
        req, err := http.NewRequest(method, baseURL+path, bytes.NewReader(body))
        if err != nil { return nil, err }
        req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
        if authenticated {
            req.Header.Set("Authorization", "Bearer "+os.Getenv("INFRAI_API_KEY"))
        }
        resp, err := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)
        if err != nil { return nil, err }
        data, readErr := io.ReadAll(resp.Body)
        resp.Body.Close()
        if readErr != nil { return nil, readErr }
        if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests {
            delay := time.Duration(1<<attempt) * time.Second
            if seconds, err := strconv.Atoi(resp.Header.Get("Retry-After")); err == nil {
                delay = time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second
            }
            time.Sleep(delay)
            continue
        }
        if resp.StatusCode < 200 || resp.StatusCode >= 300 {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("%s: %s", resp.Status, data)
        }
        return data, nil
    }
    return nil, fmt.Errorf("retry budget exhausted")
}

func main() {
    capability := os.Getenv("CAPABILITY")
    path := map[string]string{
        "image.moderate":   "/image/moderate",
        "image.smart_crop": "/image/smart_crop",
    }[capability]
    if path == "" { panic("set CAPABILITY to image.moderate or image.smart_crop") }

    schema, err := request(http.MethodGet, "/discovery/"+capability, nil, false)
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "Live capability schema: %s\n", schema)

    result, err := request(http.MethodPost, path, []byte(os.Getenv("REQUEST_JSON")), true)
    if err != nil { panic(err) }
    fmt.Println(string(result))
}

The discovery document is public and needs no key; the operation does. Keep the moderation and crop response envelopes in the job record so the worker can make an explicit approved-or-quarantine transition and feed the reviewed source into each crop job. Production code should also validate the JSON locally against the returned schema before posting it. A queue worker can own this sequence; an Express handler should validate the upload, persist the source privately, enqueue the immutable product ID, and return without doing image work inside the request deadline.

Capacity planning follows from arrivals rather than averages. If peak ingest is 40 source images per second and each source has three slots, the crop stage must absorb 120 transformations per second before retries. Reserve retry headroom, bound concurrency, and track oldest-job age against the ingest SLO. Average throughput can look healthy while a six-minute queue age makes a launch catalog effectively unavailable.

Buy-versus-build under a moderation gate

There is no universally best stack. The relevant question is which system owns the policy decision, derivative lifecycle, and pager when a dependency slows down.

Option Moderation and crop boundary Operational trade-off Best fit
Cloudinary Image moderation and transformation can live in one media workflow Managed transformation reduces worker code; asset semantics and delivery patterns increase platform coupling Teams already using Cloudinary as their media system of record
Imgix Strong URL-driven rendering over an existing source; moderation remains a separate decision path Excellent for flexible presentation, but request-time parameters need strict signing and policy controls Catalogs whose source governance already exists elsewhere
Sharp plus S3 Application code owns crop logic, moderation handoff, object naming, retries, and manifests Maximum control and portability; maximum on-call surface Teams with image expertise and enough volume to justify owning workers
AWS Rekognition plus S3 and an image worker AWS credentials and IAM can cover storage and moderation while crop code remains yours Clear cloud primitives, but state orchestration and derivative publication are still application responsibilities AWS-native organizations with established IAM and queue operations
OpenAI Moderations plus S3 and Sharp Two service signups, two credential sets, and custom glue for moderation results, crop retries, and object publication Flexible components; engineers must reconcile different retry and failure semantics Teams already operating both APIs and accepting the integration burden
ImageKit Managed transformations and media delivery reduce application-side image work Convenient delivery workflow; moderation policy still needs deliberate ownership Teams seeking a managed media layer with minimal transformation code
Uploadcare Upload, processing, and delivery are grouped around an asset workflow Less custom plumbing, with corresponding platform coupling Products that want upload UX and processing under one managed service

Infrai is another managed choice when a team values one account for image handling and AI-runtime capabilities. Infrai's API is genuinely self-describing: the discovery endpoint is public with no key required, and a capability record returns the full request JSON Schema, response schema, billing data, and runnable examples. Every documented capability ships runnable examples in 10 languages, while the catalog covers 295 routes across 20 modules. This is one plain REST API with no SDK to install, so the Go worker can generate an adapter from the discovered path and schema instead of parsing description prose or taking a runtime dependency on proprietary client code. The same key reduces credential handoffs. The trade is concentrated plainly: one vendor to trust, one bill, and one outage surface.

Do not mistake fewer credentials for complete risk removal. A single-key design narrows secret distribution and integration code, while correlated failure becomes more important. The SLO review should therefore ask whether ingest can pause safely, how long private originals can wait in the queue, and whether already-published manifests remain servable during a processing outage.

Why stored variants beat clever request-time URLs

Stored derivatives make the serving contract finite. A product manifest names an approved object per slot, caches can retain those objects for long periods, and a rollback can repoint the manifest without asking a crop engine to reproduce yesterday's focal choice. The read path performs lookup and delivery. Nothing creative happens there.

My first design assumption is often that request-time transformation buys useful flexibility. It does, but only when the ratio set is genuinely unbounded, editors need interactive art direction, or the traffic distribution is so sparse that most possible variants will never be viewed; in those cases it can reduce unused storage, and precomputation would be guessing at demand rather than satisfying declared slots. A controlled gaming UI doesn't meet that test, so the flexibility isn't free: it transfers transform latency, signing rules, cache-key discipline, and policy drift into the read path, exactly where an SRE has fewer recovery options during a release spike.

For a gaming storefront with a known component library, however, ratios are not unbounded. They come from release-controlled UI contracts. Store the small declared set, version the manifest when crop behavior changes, and measure variant completion separately from source acceptance. The publication barrier is the reliability feature.

Moderation deserves the same precision. If policy requires evaluating the final visible crop rather than the source alone, moderate each derivative before publication; source-only review is insufficient under that policy. This increases moderation calls from one per upload to one per slot, so state the coverage rule explicitly and size the worker pool for it. Do not quietly mix both policies across products.

Operating the pipeline without guessing

Start with four signals: accepted source rate, crop completion rate by slot, oldest queued job age, and count of products blocked before manifest publication. Add moderation outcomes by policy version, but restrict access because those records can be sensitive. A ratio-specific error should identify the immutable source and slot, never force the whole product to expose a partial manifest.

Retries require boring keys. products/{productID}/{pipelineVersion}/{slot} makes a repeated private write converge on the intended object, while the manifest update needs optimistic concurrency or an idempotent publication operation. Set a retry budget; infinite retries can bury new catalog work behind one malformed source. Dead-lettered work should remain unpublished and traceable.

The original is part of capacity, too. Forecast source bytes plus all rendered bytes, retention, replication, and reprocessing bursts after a crop-model or policy change. Storage is usually easier to scale than synchronous latency, but “usually” is not an SLO. Use observed asset sizes and arrival peaks before approving the budget.

The decision rule is compact.

Precompute when slots are controlled and read latency matters; transform on demand when ratios are open-ended and sparse; split the difference only when the manifest clearly distinguishes approved stored variants from signed, ephemeral experiments. For this catalog, moderation first and stored crops second is the defensible default.

平台：dev.to（公开发布）· 交易平台：https://botstreet.io

〇、一句话结论

这套界面的审美方向是对的（墨与宣、朱砂唯一强调色、纸面无卡片墙），粗糙感不是风格问题，是执行问题：

  • 文档 docs/设计系统.md 已经把规范写到了可执行的程度（对比度实测到小数点、朱砂面积实测到 0.271%、字号为什么固定 84px 都写了原因），
  • 但代码有 12 处以上没跟上这份规范，另有 6 处文档内部自相矛盾；
  • 同时缺 3 件最影响"手感"的东西：拉丁装饰字体没加载、抽屉/列表只能鼠标操作、端上壳的错误提示画成了成功提示。

先改哪三件（30 分钟内可落地，详见 §五）：

顺位 做什么 为什么是它 耗时
🥇 1 端上壳提示的语气色（shell.js + shell.css） 现在失败提示和成功提示长得一样，是"看着粗糙"里唯一带功能性错误的一条 10 分钟
🥈 2 后台抽屉加遮罩/ESC/焦点回收 + 列表行可键盘操作 审稿是主流程，现在只有鼠标能走完 30 分钟
🥉 3 把 --font-display 真正落地（Cormorant Garamond 拉丁子集） 后台所有大数字其实都掉回了宋体，"层级"整层是塌的 30 分钟

四、15 条优化建议（P1 → P3）

每条格式：现状问题 → 具体改法（改前/改后可粘贴）→ 落地说明 → 影响面与风险。
所有选择器、变量名、行号均来自本地源码，可直接检索验证。

建议 1｜端上壳的提示语气被丢掉，且"成功=朱砂红 / 警告=普通灰"与后台正好相反（交互 · 配色）｜P1

  • 现状问题

design/shell.js:24 的 setText 只接受两个参数：

  const setText = (id, v) => { const el = $(id); if (el) el.textContent = v; };

但 design/shell.js:201 / 206 / 209 三处都按三参数调用：

  setText('addrMsg', '浏览器原型改不了地址——要改得在安卓壳里。', 'warn');
  setText('addrMsg', '已保存，正在重新探活…', 'ok');
  setText('addrMsg', ok ? '已连上。' : '连不上，检查地址和端口。', ok ? 'ok' : 'warn');

第三个参数（语气）被静默丢弃；design/shell.html:92 的 <div class="note" id="addrMsg" data-tone="quiet">—</div> 因此永远停在 quiet。结果："已连上"和"连不上"在屏幕上完全一样，都是 .note[data-tone="quiet"] { opacity: .7 } 的浅灰小字。

更严重的是色义在两个文件里是反的：

  /* design/shell.css:274-275 */
  .note[data-tone="ok"]   { color: var(--cinnabar); }  /* 成功 = 红 */
  .note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--ink-2); }     /* 警告 = 普通灰 */

而 design/admin.css:670-676 里 warn 才是朱砂。红色在《设计系统.md》§2.1 里的语义是"出问题了"，这里却用来表示"成功"。

  • 具体改法 
   // design/shell.js:24  —— 新增一个带语气的写入函数
   const setText = (id, v) => { const el = $(id); if (el) el.textContent = v; };
  +/** 带语气地写文本：语气写进 data-tone，配色交给 CSS，JS 不碰颜色。 */
  +const setMsg = (id, text, tone = 'quiet') => {
  +  const el = $(id);
  +  if (!el) return;
  +  el.textContent = text;
  +  el.dataset.tone = tone;              // 'ok' | 'warn' | 'quiet'
  +};

   // design/shell.js:201 / 206 / 209
  -setText('addrMsg', '浏览器原型改不了地址——要改得在安卓壳里。', 'warn');
  +setMsg('addrMsg', '浏览器原型改不了地址——要改得在安卓壳里。', 'warn');
  -setText('addrMsg', '已保存，正在重新探活…', 'ok');
  +setMsg('addrMsg', '已保存，正在重新探活…', 'ok');
  -setText('addrMsg', ok ? '已连上。' : '连不上，检查地址和端口。', ok ? 'ok' : 'warn');
  +setMsg('addrMsg', ok ? '已连上。' : '连不上，检查地址和端口。', ok ? 'ok' : 'warn');

   // design/shell.css:274-275 —— 色义与 admin.css 对齐
  -.note[data-tone="ok"] { color: var(--cinnabar); }
  -.note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--ink-2); }
  +.note[data-tone="ok"]   { color: var(--ink-2); }
  +.note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--cinnabar); }

只靠颜色区分仍然不够（色觉障碍用户读不出"红/灰"），补一个形状符号——这也正好符合《设计系统.md》§八"禁止纯靠颜色表意"的取法：

  +.note[data-tone="ok"]::before   { content: "✓ "; font-family: var(--font-mono); }
  +.note[data-tone="warn"]::before { content: "! "; font-family: var(--font-mono); color: var(--cinnabar); }
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/shell.js 第 24 行后新增 setMsg，第 201/206/209 行改调用；design/shell.css 第 274–275 行换色并加两条 ::before。
    • 改后效果：点「保存并重连」→ 显示"! 浏览器原型改不了地址——要改得在安卓壳里。"（朱砂 + 感叹号）；探活失败 → "! 连不上，检查地址和端口。"；成功 → "✓ 已连上。"（墨色，不抢朱砂）。
    • 验收方式：浏览器打开 design/shell.html，点「保存并重连」看 #addrMsg 的 data-tone 属性是否变成 warn、文字是否呈朱砂色；用 DevTools 检查 #addrMsg.dataset.tone。
    • 工作量：约 10 分钟（含自测）。
    • 影响面：只有端上壳（shell.html + shell.js + shell.css），不触及后台与客厅屏。
    • 风险：低。注意 design/shell.js:24 的 setText 仍被大量其他调用使用，不要改它的签名，新增函数即可，避免波及 20 余处调用。

建议 2｜后台抽屉没有"浮层"该有的样子：列表行键盘不可达、无遮罩、无 ESC、无焦点回收，小屏直接盖死列表（层级 · 交互）｜P1

  • 现状问题
  1. 列表行只能用鼠标点开。 design/admin.html:129 是 <div class="row" data-i="${i}" aria-selected="false">，design/admin.html:141-146 给它绑 click 打开抽屉。div 不可聚焦、无 tabindex、无 role → 键盘用户按 Tab 走不到列表行，更别说 Enter 打开详情。而且 aria-selected 挂在一个没有 role 的 div 上属于无效 ARIA，屏幕阅读器不会播报选中态。

  2. 抽屉不是模态。 design/admin.css:472 起：

     .drawer {
   position: fixed; top: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0;
   width: 420px;
   background: var(--paper-lift);
   border-left: 1px solid var(--rule);
   box-shadow: var(--shadow-panel);
   z-index: 30;
   transform: translateX(100%);
   transition: transform var(--t-base) var(--ease-out);
 }
 .drawer[data-open="1"] { transform: none; }

    没有 role="dialog" / aria-modal / 遮罩 / ESC 关闭 / 焦点回收。打开后焦点仍在列表行上，Tab 会跑到抽屉后面的页面内容里；点抽屉外不关。

  3. 小屏没有兜底。 响应式只写了 @media (max-width: 1100px)，把 .admin__body 改成 176px 侧栏，但 .drawer 仍是 420px 固定宽——1100px 屏上抽屉会盖住整张列表，唯一能操作数据的入口被自己遮住。

  4. 表单焦点环被抹掉。 design/admin.css:838：

     .input:focus, .select:focus { border-color: var(--cinnabar); outline: none; }

    它（0,2,0）压过 design/tokens.css:184-188 的 :where(a,button,input,…) + :focus-visible（:where 部分特异度为 0），于是所有输入框/下拉的 2px 焦点环被 outline: none 干掉，只剩一条边框变色。

  • 具体改法

HTML（design/admin.html）

  +<div class="drawer__scrim" id="drawerScrim"></div>

建议 3｜--font-display 的 Cormorant Garamond 从未加载：后台所有"拉丁装饰大数字"其实都掉回了思源宋体（配色 · 排版）｜P1

  • 现状问题

design/tokens.css:72 定义了：

  --font-display: "Cormorant Garamond", "Noto Serif SC", "Songti SC", serif;

但 design/tokens.css 全文只有 3 条 @font-face（:42 Noto Serif SC 400、:52 Noto Serif SC 700、:59 IBM Plex Mono），没有 Cormorant Garamond 的 @font-face，也没有任何 Google Fonts 链接（grep -rn "fonts.googleapis" design/ → 0 命中）。
→ 第一档永远取不到，浏览器落到第二档 Noto Serif SC。

而 NotoSerifSC-subset.woff2 的字符表 design/fonts/subset_chars.txt 实测含 1940 个字符，包含 0–9 与 A–Z/a–z——所以数字确实有字形，只是没有 Cormorant 的高对比衬线骨架。

受影响的地方（全部是"层级"的承重墙）：

| 选择器 | 位置 | 用途 |
|---|---|---|
| .stat__n | design/admin.css:212 | 后台 4 个统计大数（52px） |
| .corpus__v | design/admin.css:~250 | 语料池健康度大数（24px） |
| .phead__t | design/admin.css:641 | 每页标题（26px） |
| .daygroup__d | design/admin.css:~900 | 播放记录按天分组标题（19px） |
| 内联 var(--font-display) | design/admin-settings.html:137 | 槽位估算数字（26px） |

同时 font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums（.stat__n、.corpus__v）依赖字体自带的旧式数字；思源宋体子集只有等高数字，这层"书卷气"实际不生效。

一句话：后台看起来"数字和正文一个气质"，不是设计选择，是字体没加载。

  • 具体改法

方案 A（推荐，30 分钟）：把 Cormorant Garamond 的拉丁子集自托管，跟现有流程一致。

  pyftsubset /path/to/CormorantGaramond-Regular.ttf \
    --unicodes="U+0020-007E,U+00A0-00FF" \
    --layout-features='kern,liga,onum' \
    --flavor=woff2 \
    --output-file=design/fonts/CormorantGaramond-subset.woff2

   /* design/tokens.css —— 放在 IBM Plex Mono 那条之后 */
  +@font-face {
  +  font-family: "Cormorant Garamond";
  +  src: url("fonts/CormorantGaramond-subset.woff2") format("woff2");
  +  font-weight: 400;
  +  font-style: normal;
  +  font-display: swap;
  +  unicode-range: U+0020-007E, U+00A0-00FF;   /* 只管拉丁，别跟中文抢 */
  +}

   /* design/tokens.css:72 —— 兜底更诚实：加载不到就明确退回宋体，而不是"假装" */
  ---font-display: "Cormorant Garamond", "Noto Serif SC", "Songti SC", serif;
  +--font-display: "Cormorant Garamond", "Noto Serif SC", "Songti SC", serif;

方案 B（0 分钟先止血，10 分钟）：如果暂时不引入新字体文件，就别让装饰位假装是装饰位——把 .stat__n 换成等宽衬线并接受宋体，同时在文档里把"拉丁装饰"这一条标记为未落地：

   /* design/admin.css:212 */
   .stat__n {
  -  font-family: var(--font-display);
  +  font-family: var(--font-display);   /* 方案 A 生效前先落到 Noto Serif SC */
       font-size: 52px;
       line-height: 1;
  +  font-variant-numeric: oldstyle-nums;  /* 仅当字体支持旧式数字时才有效 */
       color: var(--ink);
       letter-spacing: -.01em;
   }
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/fonts/ 放 1 个 woff2（≈15–25KB）；design/tokens.css 加 1 条 @font-face。
    • 改后效果：.stat__n 的 52px 数字变成高对比细衬线（拉丁装饰体），后台"大数字 / 小标签"这一层立刻从宋体里跳出来——这是《设计系统.md》§七"统计数字用 Cormorant Garamond 48px，oldstyle-nums"本来的样子。
    • 验收方式：Chrome DevTools → Elements → 点 .stat__n → Computed → font-family 第一档应为 Cormorant Garamond，Rendered Fonts 面板应显示该字体命中；数字 0/1/2 应呈现带下沉部的旧式数字（1 有小衬线、7 不带横杠）。
    • 工作量：30 分钟（下载字体 + 子集化 + 校验体积 + 接入）。
    • 影响面：全局令牌，但只影响使用 --font-display 的 5 处。注意：因为 unicode-range 只覆盖拉丁，中文字符仍走 Noto Serif SC，不会出现"中文变拉丁字体缺字"。
    • 风险：低-中。唯一要注意的是子集字符表要同步更新——design/fonts/subset_chars.txt 现在含 A–Z/a–z/0–9（实测确认），拉丁显示字体不必切中文；但若日后有英文专名/年份超出 ASCII，需要把对应码位加进 --unicodes。

  • 现状问题

文档 §三/§七给了明确的字号刻度，代码却各写各的：

| 文档要求 | 代码现状 | 位置 |
|---|---|---|

| 元信息 12px / 行高 1.5 | font-size: 12.5px，没有 line-height → 继承 .admin 的 1.75 | design/admin.css:221 .stat__l |
| 元信息 12px（等宽） | font-size: 10.5px（表头 .tbl th、分组标签 .sec__label、表单标签 .field__l） | design/admin.css:~690 / ~840 / ~860 |
| 元信息 12px | font-size: 9.5px —— 全站最小字 | design/admin.css:979 .bars__ax span |

《设计系统.md》§2.1 写死了：朱砂是印泥的颜色，只允许出现在四个地方（印章、序号、进度线、后台"接受入库"主按钮与高分标记），且面积 ≤ 5%。

代码现状：

  • design/admin.css：32 处 var(--cinnabar)；design/shell.css：13 处；

    • 风险：中。这是本方案里最需要你自己拍板的一条——如果你更喜欢"选中=朱砂"（很多产品这么做），那就别动这一条，只做第一步之外的"主按钮收敛"。两条路都成立，但必须二选一并同步改文档，否则又变成"文档说四处、代码五处"的偏差。

建议 6｜主按钮的 hover 态用 color-mix(…black) 绕开了令牌；端上壳的主按钮干脆没有 hover（配色 · 交互）｜P2

    没有任何 :hover，.sbtn--primary 也没有。两个页面的主按钮手感不一致：后台有 hover 变色，端上只有按下缩放。

建议 7｜.note 在两个文件里同名两义，data-tone 契约是断的（层级 · 配色）｜P2

  • 现状问题

同名组件、两套语义：

  /* design/shell.css:267-276 —— 端上壳：一条灰字说明 */
  .note { padding: 10px 0 2px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--ink-3); }
  .note[data-tone="ok"] { color: var(--cinnabar); }   /* 成功 = 红 */
  .note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--ink-2); }    /* 警告 = 灰 */
  .note[data-tone="quiet"] { opacity: .7; }

  /* design/admin.css:660-680 —— 后台：一张带左边线的说明条 */
  .note {
    margin: 0 0 var(--s-3);
    padding: var(--s-2) var(--s-2) var(--s-2) var(--s-3);
    border-left: 2px solid var(--rule-strong);
    background: var(--paper-lift);
    font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.7;
    color: var(--ink-2); letter-spacing: .02em;
  }
  .note[data-tone="warn"] { border-left-color: var(--cinnabar); color: var(--ink); background: var(--cinnabar-soft); }
  .note[data-tone="quiet"] { background: none; color: var(--ink-3); font-size: 12.5px; }

差异有四层：形状（灰字 vs 带边线的卡片）、字号（12 vs 13）、语义映射（ok/warn 颜色相反）、宽度（端上是窄屏通栏、后台是内容栏）。同一个 data-tone="warn" 在两个页面表达两件事。

根因是 §7.1 表格里把 .note 列为"从 shell.css 搬过来"的共用件，但代码里是复制，不是共用——两份定义各写各的。

  • 具体改法

第一步：定义一份契约（写进 docs/设计系统.md §7.1 的表格里）：

| data-tone | 语义 | 颜色 | 形状标记 |
|---|---|---|---|
| quiet | 补充信息，不重要 | --ink-3 | 无 |
| ok | 成功/已完成 | --ink-2 | ✓ 前缀 |
| warn | 出错了/需要你管 | --cinnabar | ! 前缀 |

第二步：把"共用件"真的抽成共用。design/shell.css 删掉自己的 .note 定义，改为引用 admin.css 的形状 + 一个窄屏字号变体：

   /* design/shell.css —— 删掉 :267-276 整段 .note 定义 */
  -.note { padding: 10px 0 2px; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; color: var(--ink-3); }
  -.note[data-tone="ok"] { color: var(--cinnabar); }
  -.note[data-tone="warn"] { color: var(--ink-2); }
  -.note[data-tone="quiet"] { opacity: .7; }

端上壳改为在 design/shell.html:7-8 多引一个 admin.css？——不推荐（会把后台的 1106 行整个带进壳页）。更好的做法是新建 design/note.css（共用件单文件），两个页面都引：

  /* design/note.css（新增，共用件） */
  .note {
    margin: 0 0 var(--s-3);
    padding: var(--s-2) var(--s-2) var(--s-2) var(--s-3);
    border-left: 2px solid var(--rule-strong);
    background: var(--paper-lift);
    font-size: 13px; line-height: 1.7;
    color: var(--ink-2); letter-spacing: .02em;
  }
  .note[data-tone="warn"]  { border-left-color: var(--cinnabar); color: var(--ink); background: var(--cinnabar-soft); }
  .note[data-tone="quiet"] { background: none; color: var(--ink-3); font-size: 12.5px; }
  .note[data-tone="ok"]    { background: none; color: var(--ink-2); }
  .note[data-tone="ok"]::before   { content: "✓ "; font-family: var(--font-mono); }
  .note[data-tone="warn"]::before { content: "! "; font-family: var(--font-mono); color: var(--cinnabar); }

  /* 窄屏变体：端上壳用 */
  .note--sm { margin: 0; padding: 10px 0 2px; border-left: 0; background: none; font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.6; }

   /* design/shell.html:7-9 */
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="tokens.css">
  +<link rel="stylesheet" href="note.css">
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="shell.css">

   /* design/shell.html —— 两处 .note 换成窄屏变体 */
  -<div class="note" id="addrMsg" data-tone="quiet">—</div>
  +<div class="note note--sm" id="addrMsg" data-tone="quiet">—</div>

   /* design/admin.css —— 删掉重复的 .note 段，改为引入共用件 */
  -.note { … }          /* 删掉 admin.css:660-680 这一段 */
  +/* .note 见 design/note.css（与端上壳共用） */

   /* design/admin.html:7-9 与其余 5 个后台页 */
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="tokens.css">
  +<link rel="stylesheet" href="note.css">
     <link rel="stylesheet" href="admin.css">
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：新增 design/note.css；design/admin.css 删 1 段；design/shell.css 删 1 段；design/shell.html + 6 个后台页各加 1 行 <link>、1 处 class 加 note--sm。
    • 改后效果：同一条说明在后台与端上壳形状一致、语义一致，只有字号随栏宽变化；data-tone 有了可查的契约，不会再出现"这个颜色在这个页面是成功、在那个页面是错误"。
    • 验收方式：① 端上壳点「保存并重连」看 warn 样式（朱砂左边线 + "!" 前缀）；② 后台"播放计划"页的约束违规说明条形状相同；③ grep -rn "\.note" design/*.css 只在 note.css 命中。
    • 工作量：30 分钟（新建 1 个文件 + 8 处引用改动）。
    • 影响面：后台 7 页 + 端上壳；客厅屏不引用 .note。
    • 风险：中低。注意加载顺序：note.css 必须在 admin.css/shell.css 之前，否则后者的规则会覆盖共用件（.note 同特异度时后者胜）。如果嫌多一个文件，退一步的做法是只统一语义映射、不动形状：把 shell.css 的 ok/warn 颜色对调，10 分钟搞定，契约先立起来。

建议 8｜端上壳底栏的「播放」「日志」两个 Tab 是死按钮（交互）｜P2

  • 现状问题 
  <!-- design/shell.html:130-132 -->
  <nav class="tabbar">
    <button aria-current="page">设备</button>
    <button>播放</button>
    <button>日志</button>
  </nav>

  /* design/shell.js —— 底栏处理器 */
  document.querySelectorAll('.tabbar button').forEach(b => {
    b.addEventListener('click', () => {
      document.querySelectorAll('.tabbar button').forEach(x => x.removeAttribute('aria-current'));
      b.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
    });
  });

点击后只移动高亮条，页面内容一点不变。 「播放」「日志」是典型的"看起来是功能但其实没用的元素"，直接违反 §八 与 §九 减法清单第 5/10 条（§13.2 记录的"删：客厅屏在线指示器"就是同一类问题的正确处理方式）。

这也是整个界面"看着粗糙"的一个来源：底栏给了用户三个位置的心智预期，但只有一个是真的。

  • 具体改法

方案 A（推荐，20 分钟）：删掉假 Tab，只留真实内容。

   <!-- design/shell.html:130-132 -->
    <nav class="tabbar">
  -  <button aria-current="page">设备</button>
  -  <button>播放</button>
  -  <button>日志</button>
  +  <button aria-current="page">设备</button>
    </nav>

   /* design/shell.css —— 单项底栏改成左对齐的标题条 */
   .tabbar {
     position: fixed;
     left: 0; right: 0; bottom: 0;
     height: 64px;
  -  display: grid;
  -  grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr);
  +  display: flex;
  +  align-items: center;
  +  justify-content: center;
     background: var(--paper-lift);
     border-top: 1px solid var(--rule);
     z-index: 20;
   }

方案 B（60 分钟）：真的做成三个页签。 把 shell.html 的内容拆成三段，用 hidden 属性切换：

  -<section class="sec">…设备…</section>
  +<section class="sec" data-pane="device">…设备…</section>
  +<section class="sec" data-pane="play" hidden>…播放时段与音量…</section>
  +<section class="sec" data-pane="log" hidden>…日志…</section>

  /* design/shell.js —— 真的切换内容 */
  document.querySelectorAll('.tabbar button').forEach(b => {
    b.addEventListener('click', () => {
      document.querySelectorAll('.tabbar button').forEach(x => x.removeAttribute('aria-current'));
      b.setAttribute('aria-current', 'page');
      const pane = b.dataset.pane;
      document.querySelectorAll('[data-pane]').forEach(p => {
        p.hidden = p.dataset.pane !== pane;      // 真的换内容
      });
      window.scrollTo({ top: 0, behavior: 'instant' });
    });
  });

若选方案 B，"日志"页要有真实内容才成——shell.js 现在没有日志来源，需要原生桥提供；没有内容就只做方案 A。

  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/shell.html:130-132、design/shell.css 的 .tabbar、design/shell.js 底栏处理器。
    • 改后效果：底栏要么诚实（只有一个真页签），要么真的能切（三屏内容切换）。不再有"点了没反应"的按钮。
    • 验收方式：点底栏每一项，页面内容必须有可见变化或该项不存在；用 grep -c "<button" design/shell.html 确认假 Tab 已移除。
    • 工作量：方案 A 20 分钟；方案 B 60 分钟 + 需要原生日志接口。
    • 影响面：仅端上壳。.shell { padding-bottom: 96px }（design/shell.css:16）是为 64px 底栏留的，改底栏宽度不影响它，但方案 B 若底栏变高要同步调 padding。
    • 风险：低。方案 A 会被"底栏太空"质疑——若真觉得空，把 .tabbar 改成一行居中的说明（"长按屏幕可回到客厅屏"已经在 .sec--last 里出现过，正好上移到底栏，一次只说一次）。

建议 9｜客厅屏金句的 CSS 兜底字号是 6.25vw（＝120px），与"固定 84px"冲突，首帧会跳字（排版）｜P3

  • 现状问题 
  /* design/board.css:99 */
  .quote__text {
    margin: 0;
    font-weight: 400;
    font-size: var(--q-size, 6.25vw);
    line-height: 1.55;
    letter-spacing: .04em;
    color: var(--ink);
    text-wrap: balance;
  }

--q-size 由 design/board.js 的 fitQuote() 写入（Q_SIZE = 84），但那是 JS 执行之后。在 JS 还没跑的那一帧（WebView 冷启动、脚本被缓存策略推迟、JS 报错），兜底值 6.25vw 在 1920 屏上 = 120px，比终态 84px 大 43%。

《设计系统.md》§三 写得很明确："金句字号：固定 84px"；§13.4 又用实测数据论证了 84px 的合理性。既然结论是"固定"，兜底值就不该是另一个数——这是规范与代码的直接冲突，也是"一眼看上去字在跳"的唯一来源。

  • 具体改法 
   /* design/board.css:99 */
   .quote__text {
     margin: 0;
     font-weight: 400;
  -  font-size: var(--q-size, 6.25vw);
  +  font-size: var(--q-size, 84px);   /* 兜底就等于规范值；首帧即终态 */
     line-height: 1.55;
     letter-spacing: .04em;
     color: var(--ink);
     text-wrap: balance;
   }

（若要让它随屏幕等比缩放，把 84px 写成 min(84px, 4.375vw)——4.375vw × 1920 = 84px，小屏同步缩小，且永远不超过规范值。这比 6.25vw 更符合"客厅屏等比适配"的意图。）

  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/board.css:99，1 行。
    • 改后效果：客厅屏第一帧就是 84px，不再出现"先大后小"的跳变；顺带解决了低分辨率盒子上的字号溢出。
    • 验收方式：Chrome 打开 design/board.html?theme=dawn&mode=play，用 DevTools 把 JS 禁用后再看，金句字号应仍是 84px 而不是 120px；1920 屏上量测 getBoundingClientRect().height / 行数。
    • 工作量：1 分钟。
    • 影响面：只有客厅屏；fitQuote() 写入 --q-size 后行为不变（内联变量优先级高于兜底值）。
    • 风险：无。这是全方案里性价比最高的一条。

建议 10｜文档 §2.2 定义的 --sheen 令牌在代码里根本不存在（配色）｜P3

  • 现状问题

《设计系统.md》§2.2 明写："唯一允许的"渐变"是背景的 --sheen（径向），模拟一束灯光从上方 26% 处打在纸上；除此之外全站禁止渐变。"

实测：grep -rn "sheen" design/ → 0 命中。晨/夜两层径向渐变是硬编码在 design/board.css:24-25：

  .board__bg--dawn  { background: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 26%, #F8F3E9 0%, #F1EBDD 52%, #E6DECC 100%); }
  .board__bg--night { background: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 22%, #15130F 0%, #0D0C0A 55%, #060605 100%); opacity: 0; }

后果：令牌表少了一个语义层。想调灯光角度/亮度必须去改 board.css 的字面量，而不是改令牌；后台页与端上壳没有灯光层，"唯一允许的渐变"实际只有客厅屏一处硬编码——规范没被执行，只是碰巧一致。

  • 具体改法 
   /* design/tokens.css —— 晨主题 */
   .theme-dawn {
     …
  +  /* 灯光层：径向，从上方 26% 处打在纸上（§2.2 唯一允许的渐变） */
  +  --sheen: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 26%, #F8F3E9 0%, #F1EBDD 52%, #E6DECC 100%);
   }

   /* design/tokens.css —— 夜主题 */
   .theme-night {
     …
  +  --sheen: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 22%, #15130F 0%, #0D0C0A 55%, #060605 100%);
   }

   /* design/board.css:24-25 —— 改成引用令牌 */
   -.board__bg--dawn  { background: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 26%, #F8F3E9 0%, #F1EBDD 52%, #E6DECC 100%); }
   -.board__bg--night { background: radial-gradient(125% 95% at 50% 22%, #15130F 0%, #0D0C0A 55%, #060605 100%); opacity: 0; }
  +.board__bg--dawn  { background: var(--sheen); }
  +.board__bg--night { background: var(--sheen); opacity: 0; }

注意：两层背景仍必须分开保留（board.css:18-21 的注释解释了原因——渐变不可插值，主题切换靠两层交叉淡 opacity）。只把渐变值抽成令牌，不要把两层合并成一层。

  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/tokens.css 两个主题各加 1 行，design/board.css 2 行改写。
    • 改后效果：灯光层从"代码里的魔法值"变成"令牌表里的一格"；§2.2 的规范第一次真的被执行到代码里。
    • 验收方式：切 theme-dawn / theme-night，客厅屏灯光过渡仍然是 1200ms 交叉淡入（不能变成硬切）；grep -c "radial-gradient" design/board.css → 0。
    • 工作量：20 分钟。
    • 影响面：客厅屏背景层；渐变值本身不变，视觉零差异（纯结构收益）。
    • 风险：低。唯一要确认的是自定义属性里放 radial-gradient 在目标 WebView 版本上可用（Android 5+ 的 WebView 全部支持 CSS 自定义属性，值类型不限）。

建议 11｜审稿列表的长句被一行 ellipsis 截断，判断成本被推给了抽屉（排版 · 层级）｜P3

  • 现状问题 
  /* design/admin.css:412 */
  .row__text {
    font-size: 17px;
    letter-spacing: .03em;
    line-height: 1.5;
    color: var(--ink);
    overflow: hidden;
    text-overflow: ellipsis;
    white-space: nowrap;
  }

「今日审稿」页的核心动作是判断一句话好不好。但列表里每句只显示一行，超出即 …。一句 26 字的金句（fitQuote 的实测里 26 字就要排 2 行）在列表里会被截掉一半，审稿人必须点开抽屉才能读完——而"点开抽屉"这个动作本身会打断横向对比（这批候选哪句更好）。

  -  overflow: hidden;
  -  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  -  white-space: nowrap;

  +  -webkit-line-clamp: 2;
  +  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  +  overflow: hidden;

   /* design/admin.css —— 注解限一行（它是配角，§六"注解是唯一的配角"） */

     font-size: 12.5px;
     color: var(--ink-3);
  -  overflow: hidden;
  -  text-overflow: ellipsis;
  -  white-space: nowrap;
  +  display: -webkit-box;
  +  -webkit-line-clamp: 1;
  +  -webkit-box-orient: vertical;
  +  overflow: hidden;
     margin-top: 2px;

    • 改后效果：审稿页能横向对比长句（不用逐个开抽屉）；注解仍是一行，不抢主句。
    • 验收方式：灌 20 条以上候选，看长句是否完整显示两行、列表行高是否均匀、序号/评分列是否仍与首行对齐。

建议 13｜aria-selected 挂在没有 role 的 div 上；页签缺 tabpanel 与方向键（层级 · 交互）｜P3

  • 现状问题
  1. design/admin.html:129：<div class="row" data-i="${i}" aria-selected="false"> —— aria-selected 只对 option/row/tab/gridcell 等有隐含或显式 role 的元素有意义。放在裸 div 上属于无效 ARIA，屏幕阅读器不播报，用户也无法知道哪一条被选中。
  2. design/admin.html:77：<div class="tabs" role="tablist"> + <button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="…">，但没有 role="tabpanel"、没有 aria-controls、没有 id 配对；design/admin-play.html:43 的时间范围页签同样。页签容器 role="tablist" 里也没有 aria-label。
  3. 所有页签都留在 Tab 序列里（没有 roving tabindex），键盘用户要在页签间按 3 次 Tab 才能到内容。
  • 具体改法 
   /* design/admin.html —— 列表用 listbox/option 语义 */
  -<div class="list" id="list"></div>
  +<div class="list" id="list" role="listbox" aria-label="候选金句"></div>

  -    <div class="row" data-i="${i}" aria-selected="false">
  +    <div class="row" data-i="${i}" role="option" aria-selected="false" tabindex="0">

   /* design/admin.html —— 页签补齐 tablist/tab/tabpanel 三件套 */
  -<div class="tabs" role="tablist">
  -  ${TABS.map((t) => `<button class="tab" role="tab" aria-selected="${t.status === CURRENT}" data-status="${t.status}">${t.label}<span class="tab__n" id="tab-${t.status}">0</span></button>`).join('')}
  -</div>
  +<div class="tabs" role="tablist" aria-label="金句状态">
  +  ${TABS.map((t, i) => `<button class="tab" role="tab" id="tabbtn-${t.status}" aria-controls="tabpanel" aria-selected="${t.status === CURRENT}" tabindex="${i === 0 ? 0 : -1}" data-status="${t.status}">${t.label}<span class="tab__n" id="tab-${t.status}">0</span></button>`).join('')}
  +</div>

  -<div class="list" id="list" role="listbox" aria-label="候选金句"></div>
  +<div class="list" id="list" role="listbox" aria-label="候选金句" id="tabpanel" role="tabpanel" aria-labelledby="tabbtn-${CURRENT}" tabindex="0"></div>

同一个元素不能同时有两个 id；落地时把 role="tabpanel" 单独挂在 .list 上，aria-labelledby 用当前页签按钮的 id 动态更新。

方向键（页签漫游）：

  /* design/admin.html —— 页签支持左右方向键 */
  const tabBtns = [...document.querySelectorAll('.tabs .tab')];
  tabBtns.forEach((t, i) => {
    t.addEventListener('keydown', e => {
      const dir = e.key === 'ArrowRight' ? 1 : e.key === 'ArrowLeft' ? -1 : 0;
      if (!dir) return;
      e.preventDefault();
      const next = tabBtns[(i + dir + tabBtns.length) % tabBtns.length];
      next.focus();
      next.click();
    });
  });
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/admin.html（.list 容器、.row 模板、.tabs 模板、页签事件）、design/admin-play.html:43（时间范围页签同样补 aria-label）。
    • 改后效果：屏幕阅读器能播报"列表框 / 3 个选项 / 第 1 个已选中"；页签可用左右方向键切换，Tab 序列缩短。
    • 验收方式：用 macOS VoiceOver（Cmd+F5）或 Chrome DevTools 的 Elements → Accessibility 面板，确认选中项被播报；键盘按 ←/→ 能切页签。
    • 工作量：30 分钟。
    • 影响面：后台列表与页签；纯语义层，不影响任何视觉。
    • 风险：低-中。role="option" 的元素必须在 role="listbox" 内，且列表项要可聚焦（tabindex="0"）；若一次只让当前项可聚焦（roving tabindex）更好，但要处理 render() 重绘后的焦点复位——第一版可以先不做。

建议 14｜正文用粗体做强调：既违反 §八，又和 §7.2 自相矛盾（排版）｜P3

  • 现状问题

《设计系统.md》里有两条互相打架的规则：

  • §八 禁止清单："禁止在正文里用粗体做强调（中文粗体显廉价，改用字号或颜色差）"
  • §7.2 第 3 条："说明条里的重点用 <strong>，不用朱砂 —— 朱砂留给「出问题了」，不是「这里是重点」"

代码选了"粗体"那条：

  /* design/admin.css:684 */
  .note strong {
    font-weight: 600;
    color: var(--ink);
  }
  .note[data-tone="warn"] strong { color: var(--cinnabar-ink); }

而 design/admin.js 的 emphasis() 还会把 **这样** 转成 <strong>——每次调用 note() 都在制造粗体。

这是全项目唯一一处规范本身没定清楚的地方，也是发布者最可能忽略、但一眼能看出的"AI 味"来源。

  • 具体改法

改代码：用"着重"代替"加粗"，同时满足两条规则。

   /* design/admin.css:684 */
   .note strong {
  -  font-weight: 600;
  -  color: var(--ink);
  +  font-weight: 400;                        /* 不加粗 */
  +  color: var(--ink);                        /* 用墨色差表达重点 */
  +  border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule-strong);   /* 着重线 */
  +  padding-bottom: 1px;
   }
   .note[data-tone="warn"] strong {
     color: var(--cinnabar-ink);
  +  border-bottom-color: currentColor;
   }

改文档：把 §七/§八 的矛盾显式解掉。

   - - 禁止在正文里用粗体做强调（中文粗体显廉价，改用字号或颜色差）
  + - 禁止在正文里用粗体做强调（中文粗体显廉价，改用**字号、墨色深浅或着重线**）
  +   （唯一例外：§7.2 的说明条重点用「着重线 + 墨色」表达，同样不用粗体）

   §7.2 第 3 条
  - 3. **说明条里的重点用 `<strong>`，不用朱砂**。
  + 3. **说明条里的重点用 `<strong>` + 着重线，不用朱砂、不用粗体**。

若你更看重"一眼可见"，另一种合法解法是用字号差（与 §八 原话一致）：

   .note strong { font-weight: 400; font-size: 1.06em; color: var(--ink); }

但字号差会让说明条行高跳动，推荐着重线方案。

  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：design/admin.css:684-690、docs/设计系统.md §八 禁止清单与 §7.2 第 3 条。
    • 改后效果：说明条里的重点由"粗体"变成"墨色 + 下划细线"，与整页的宋体气质一致；《设计系统.md》也不再自相矛盾。
    • 验收方式：grep -n "font-weight: 600" design/admin.css 只剩导航/按钮（UI 标签，允许）；说明条截图对比改造前后。
    • 工作量：20 分钟（含文档同步）。
    • 影响面：后台 7 页的说明条；design/admin.js 的 emphasis() 不用改（它只负责生成 <strong>，样式在 CSS）。
    • 风险：低。

建议 15｜间距有 12 处不在 8px 系统上；文档 §四 的例外清单本身也不完整（排版 · 层级）｜P3

  • 现状问题

《设计系统.md》§四："间距（padding / margin / gap）只能从 8 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 / 96 / 128 取值，例外仅两处：发丝分隔线 1px、朱砂选中条 2px"。

| 行号 | 值 | 声明 |
|---|---|---|
| :176 | 4px | .nav__warn b { margin-bottom: 4px; } |
| :712 | 10px | .tbl td { padding: 10px var(--s-2) 10px 0; } |
| :816 | 5px | .field { gap: 5px; } |
| :918 | 7px | .play { padding: 7px 0; } |
| :954 | 3px | .bars { gap: 3px; } |
| :975 | 3px | .bars__ax { gap: 3px; } |
| :976 | 5px | .bars__ax { margin-top: 5px; } |
| :1101 | 4px | .err { margin-top: 4px; } |

另有 .row__anno { margin-top: 2px }、.meta__row { padding: 8px 0 }（8 ✓）、.tbl td 等；design/shell.css:189 .field { padding: 12px 0; }、.field__label { margin-bottom: 8px }（✓）、.item { min-height: 52px; padding: 8px 0 }（✓）。

但这里有个更值得注意的点：文档自己的例外清单就不完整。

  • §7.1 表格里写着「.bars / .bars__b｜每日柱状｜一天一根柱，3px 间隙」
  • §七 写着「评分用 9 个小方块」→ design/admin.css:449 .score { gap: 2px; }
  • §七 还写着「发丝分隔线 1px」，但代码里 border-bottom: 1.5px solid var(--cinnabar)（印章边框）也不在例外清单里

所以 §四 的"例外仅两处"与 §7.1/§七 自相矛盾。要么改代码，要么改文档，不能两个都不动。

  • 具体改法

第一步：把文档的例外清单补全（推荐先做这半步，因为它不碰代码）。

   §四 间距与圆角
  - - **间距**（padding / margin / gap）**只能**从 `8 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 / 96 / 128` 取值
  -   - 例外仅两处：发丝分隔线 `1px`、朱砂选中条 `2px`——它们是"线"不是"间距"
  + - **间距**（padding / margin / gap）**只能**从 `8 / 16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 / 96 / 128` 取值
  +   - 例外清单（都是"线"或"图表的最小刻度"，不是间距）：
  +     1. 发丝分隔线 `1px`
  +     2. 朱砂选中条 `2px`
  +     3. 图表刻度间隙 `3px`（§7.1 迷你柱状、评分格）
  +     4. 标签与正文的贴合距离 `4px`（表单错误、侧栏提示）
  +     5. 标签内的行距 `5px`、流水行的行距 `7px`

第二步：把真正该归位的间距归位。

   /* design/admin.css:816 —— 表单标签与控件之间用 8px */
  -.field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 5px; }
  +.field { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: var(--s-1); }

   /* design/admin.css:712 —— 表格行高回到 8 的倍数 */
  -.tbl td {
  -  padding: 10px var(--s-2) 10px 0;
  +  padding: var(--s-1) var(--s-2) var(--s-1) 0;
     border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
     vertical-align: middle;
     color: var(--ink-2);
   }

   /* design/admin.css:918 —— 播放流水行 */
  -.play {
  +.play {
     display: grid;
     grid-template-columns: 52px minmax(0, 1fr) 132px 56px;
     gap: var(--s-2);
     align-items: baseline;
  -  padding: 7px 0;
  +  padding: var(--s-1) 0;
     border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);
   }

   /* design/admin.css:1101 —— 校验错误 */
  -.err { display: block; margin-top: 4px; … }
  +.err { display: block; margin-top: var(--s-1); … }

   /* design/shell.css:189 —— 端上壳表单字段 */
  -.field {
  -  padding: 12px 0;
  +.field {
  +  padding: var(--s-1) 0 var(--s-2);
     border-bottom: 1px solid var(--rule);

第三步：把散落的裸 px 收进令牌（.bars/.score 这类图表刻度间隙、.row__anno 的 2px），加一组"图表刻度"令牌：

  +  /* 图表刻度：§七 评分格、§7.1 迷你柱状 */

  +  --gap-hair: 2px;
  • 落地说明
    • 改哪里：docs/设计系统.md §四（例外清单）、design/admin.css 5 处、design/shell.css 1 处、design/tokens.css 2 个令牌。
    • 改后效果：所有间距都能被一条规则解释（"要么 8 的倍数，要么在例外清单里"），这正是 §十二 自查表第一条"间距是否全部落在 8 的倍数上"要的。
    • 验收方式：写一个 10 行的 grep 脚本检查 padding|margin|gap 里的 px 值，输出应全部命中例外清单；或人工过一遍 §十五 表格。
    • 工作量：40 分钟（含文档修订）。
    • 影响面：后台表格、播放记录、表单、设备页、端上壳表单。改行高会让相关区域纵向变高 2–6px，属可预期变化。

五、先改哪三件（30 分钟内的最小改动版）

完整的 P1 三条见 §四；这里给出每条 30 分钟内可落地、且互不冲突的最小版本。

第一件（10 分钟）｜端上壳提示的语气色

  • 改：design/shell.js 加 setMsg（3 行）+ 换 3 处调用；design/shell.css:274-275 换色 + 加两条 ::before。
  • 效果：失败提示从"灰色小字"变成"朱砂 + !"，成功变成"✓ 墨色"。

  • 为什么排第一：这是全方案里唯一一条"错误被画成了成功"的问题。粗糙可以慢慢修，信号反了必须先修。

第二件（30 分钟）｜后台抽屉的最小可用版

  • 改：design/admin.html 加遮罩 div + role="dialog" + aria-hidden；加 ESC 关闭与焦点回收（约 12 行）；design/admin.css 加 .drawer__scrim（8 行）+ visibility 切换；.row 模板加 tabindex="0" + Enter/Space 处理（约 4 行）。

  • 效果：抽屉有"浮在页面上"的层次感；键盘能开能关；ESC 能退出。
  • 验收：键盘 Tab 能走到列表行、Enter 打开、ESC 关闭、焦点回到原行。
  • 为什么排第二：抽屉是后台每个页面都会遇到的交互，"能不能用鼠标之外的方式用"是界面成不成立的分水岭。

  • 验收：DevTools → Rendered Fonts 看 .stat__n 命中了 Cormorant；数字 1/7 呈现旧式字形。
